New York, Mar. 20. 

Memorial services for the late 
President of China, Dr. Sun ¥at-| 
sen, were held yesterday at In- 
ternational House in the presence 
of about 1,000 persons. The cere- 
monies were conducted in the 
Chinese manner by Mr. Yau 
Chang-fu, a merchant of this city. 

Many of the speakers were in 
native costume as they bowed be- 
fore the portrait of the first T.e- 
sident of the Republic of China. 
Some bore fruit to symbolize the 
riches he tried to bring to the 
400,000,000 inhabitants of his 
country; while others brought flow- 
ers as tributes to his lifelong 
labours which ended on March 12 
in the city of Peking; and last, 
imcense was burned to portray the 
prayers of his followers for the 
prosperity of the Chinese people. 
This portrait was draped with the 
five coloured. flag cf China. ; 

The speakers were Mr. Lung: 
Chi-lo, Prof. John Deway, Mr. 
Taraknath Das, Mr. Ernest K. 
Moy and Mr. Paul Linebarger, the 
biographer of Dr. Sun Yat-sen.! 
Mr. Linebarger said: “In my 
work with the great Chinese re- 
former I know that he drew his 
inspiration not from the life of 
Alexander the Great, not from 
Caesar, not from Charlemagne, not 
from Napoleon, but from our own 
Washington and Lincoln. There 
never lived a more unselfish man’ 
than Dr. Sun Yat-sen. if 
Washington and Lincoln were here 
to-day they would say, “This man} 
was our brother and one of the’ 
greatest men of all time.’” 

The memorial service was held 
under the auspices of a committee 
composed of Miss Grace Li, 
daughter of Mr. Li Yuan-hung, 
formerly President of China; Miss 
Nora, daughter of an ex-premier;- 
Mrs. Ma Soo, daughter of Dr. 
Sun’s representative in this coun. 
try, and a number of prominent. 
Chinese bankers and merchants.—'

DR. SUN'S PRAISES
SUNG IN U. S.

Eulogistic Addresses
Made At Memorial
Service

New York, Mar. 20.
Memorial services for the late
President of China, Dr. Sun Yat-
sen, were held yesterday at In-
ternational House in the presence
of about 1,000 persons. The cere-
monies were conducted in the
Chinese manner by Mr. Yau
Chang-fu, a merchant of this city.
Many of the speakers were in
native costume as they bowed be-
fore the portrait of the first Pre-
sident of the Republic of China.
Some bore fruit to symbolize the
riches he tried to bring to the
400,000,000 inhabitants of his
country; while others brought flow-
ers as tributes to his lifelong
labours which ended on March 12
in the city of Peking; and last,
incense was burned to portray the
prayers of his followers for the
prosperity of the Chinese people.
This portrait was draped with the
five coloured flag of China.
The speakers were Mr. Lung
Chi-lo, Prof. John Dewey, Mr.
Taraknath Das, Mr. Ernest K.
Moy and Mr. Paul Linebarger, the
biographer of Dr. Sun Yat-sen.
Mr. Linebarger said: "In my
work with the great Chinese re-
former I know that he drew his
inspiration not from the life of
Alexander the Great, not from
Caesar, not from Charlemagne, not
from Napoleon, but from our own
Washington and Lincoln. There
never lived a more unselfish man
than Dr. Sun Yat-sen. If
Washington and Lincoln were here
to-day they would say, "This man
was our brother and one of the
greatest men of all time.'"
The memorial service was held
under the auspices of a committee
composed of Miss Grace Li,
daughter of Mr. Li Yuan-hung,
formerly President of China; Miss
Nora, daughter of an ex-premier;
Mrs. Ma Soo, daughter of Dr.
Sun's representative in this coun-
try, and a number of prominent
Chinese bankers and merchants.—
Reuter's American Service.

孙中山博士在美国获颂扬

追悼会上发表的
颂词

纽约，3月20日电。昨日，为已故中国大总统孙中山博士举行的追悼仪式在国际学社（International House）举行，约有1,000人出席。仪式由本市商人姚昌甫（Yau Chang-fu，音译）先生按中式礼仪主持。许多演讲者在向中华民国首任大总统的遗像鞠躬时，身着本国传统服装。一些人携带水果，象征他试图为其国家四亿居民带来的财富；另一些人带来鲜花，以致敬他毕生的辛劳，这些辛劳于3月12日在北京画下句点；最后，焚香以表达其追随者为中国人民繁荣所致的祈祷。遗像上覆盖着中国五色旗。

演讲者包括龙积之（Lung Chi-lo，音译）先生、约翰·杜威（John Dewey）教授、塔拉克纳特·达斯（Taraknath Das）先生、欧内斯特·K·莫伊（Ernest K. Moy）先生以及孙中山博士的传记作者保罗·莱恩巴格（Paul Linebarger）先生。莱恩巴格先生说：“在与这位伟大的中国改革家共事的过程中，我深知他的灵感并非来自亚历山大大帝、凯撒、查理曼或拿破仑的生平，而是来自我们自己的华盛顿和林肯。从未有过比孙中山博士更无私的人。如果华盛顿和林肯今日尚在人世，他们会说：‘此人是我们的兄弟，也是史上最伟大的人物之一。’”

此次追悼会由一个委员会主办，该委员会成员包括中国前总统黎元洪先生之女李格雷斯（Grace Li）小姐、一位前总理之女诺拉（Nora）小姐、孙中山博士驻美代表马素（Ma Soo，音译）博士之女马素夫人，以及多位知名中国银行家和商人。——路透社美国分社。
